prompt: The Malay Archipelago, which consists of the islands that make up the modern day Philippines, Indonesia, Malaysia, Brunei, East Timor and Papua New Guinea, are mostly inhabited by the Austronesian peoples. However, there were already humans that lived in these islands prior to the Austronesian expansion and the preceding settlement of the Proto-Malays that came before the expansion. Who were these people that lived in these islands before the Austronesians?
judge_reasoning: Candidate 1 best answers the question by identifying the two main pre-Austronesian groups commonly discussed for the region (Negrito hunter-gatherers and Austro-Melanesian/Papuan-related populations) without relying heavily on questionable named entities. Candidate 4 is also on-topic and gives several commonly cited Negrito subgroup names, but includes some dubious/location-misattribution-style statements (e.g., Senoi placement) and more speculative phrasing. Candidate 3 drifts more into speculative, loosely connected ancestry claims (e.g., Denisovans/Paleosiberians) with very specific early dates. Candidate 2 is weakest because it includes multiple high-suspicion, possibly fabricated specifics (e.g., “Homo sapiens timorensis,” and the Proto-Malays timeframe/ancestry claims) even though it is otherwise aligned with the Negrito idea.
